title: Music in a Dark Room
chapters: On Friday, Mina carried her guitar to school. Joon had a small drum, and Sara had a box of bells. Their class planned a music show for the families. Ms Park opened the music room and asked the team to enter.

The children held to one good rule: the children had to listen. Mina played fast, but Joon played slow. Sara asked them to stand back from the problem and hear the full music. The three parts did not match.
Ms Park met with the team at a round table. She opened out a large paper plan. Mina wanted the guitar to be loud, and Joon wanted the drum to be loud. Sara wrote the ideas on the paper.

They walked through the opening music with Ms Park. Mina began with only her guitar, Joon came in later, and Sara played the bells at the end. The new order brought back a happy school memory for Ms Park. She smiled and asked them to play it again.

At the end of practice, the team planned on one hour in the morning. They tidied up the room and signed out the guitar and drum. Mina and Joon headed off for home. Sara stayed to check the paper plan.
The room was bright on Saturday morning. Mina put her guitar by the window, and Joon set the drum in the center. Sara spread out the paper plan on a desk. Families would arrive later in the day.

A light on the wall went dark, and the room became dark. The radio stopped, the computer stopped, and the clock stopped. The power problem was in the full school. Mina held her guitar and did not move.

Ms Park called the school office, but the office did not answer. She left a message and asked the office to phone back. Joon began to laugh, but Mina was afraid the show had to end. Sara asked the team to step back and think.

Ms Park checked on the classes. One class had light from the sun, but the music room was dark. A child from that class came to cover for Sara at the office phone. Sara went to the window and opened it.
The team talked about the show. Mina still wanted the show, and Joon agreed. The children banded together around the window. They chose to make music with the guitar, boxes, and cups.
The children ate bread and fruit, and the food filled them up. Mina played the guitar, and Joon played the box with his hands. Sara filled three cups with a little water. The cups gave new notes.
The sun warmed up the room. The guitar and cups matched up, but the box was too loud. Joon put the box on a soft blanket. The drum became warm and clear.
A young boy wanted to join, but he was nervous. Sara gave him two bells and helped him fit in. The boy stood up by Mina and played at the end of the lines. His small part made the music bright.

The team knocked about some ideas for the dark room. They could move to the garden, open the windows, or use candles. Ms Park ruled out candles because fire was dangerous. The garden was wet from rain.

Mina mixed up the opening and the ending. She stopped, laughed, and began again. Ms Park followed up on the new order with a slow practice. At lunch, their hands were tired, but the full music was ready.

At home, Mina sat up late with her guitar. She made a short video for Joon and Sara. Joon watched it on his phone and saw that Mina played one part too fast. He called Mina and asked her to slow down.
Sara practiced the cups in her kitchen. Her mother asked her to top up the water in one cup. The new note was better. Sara gave the team a video.
Joon had to fix up the old drum. A small part was not strong, and the drum made bad music. His father helped with the work. Joon played a quiet beat and heard a clean note.
The videos helped the team even out the music. Mina made the fast part slow, and Sara made one note high. Joon held the beat slow. Their three homes had the same music.
That evening, Ms Park called the children and asked about the work. Mina gave her the new order. Ms Park told the children to sleep. The show was not perfect, but it was honest and ready.
A school bus pulled up with some families. The sky was cloudy, and the school was still dark. Ms Park took the visitors to the music room. Light came from the large windows.
Mina, Joon, Sara, and the young boy took their places. Mina felt nervous and held in a cry. Sara touched Mina's hand. Joon counted with his hands, and the music began.
The guitar was quiet, the box drum was deep, and the cups were clear. The bells came in at the right time. New families came to the door, but the children carried on. The room became full.
During the show, the power came back. The computer began to play loud music. Ms Park turned it off, and the children did not stop. Their music was strong, and the machine was not strong.
The bell ended the show. The families gave the children a loud, happy call. Mina looked at her team and laughed. The hard practice had paid off, and the dark room felt bright.

On Monday, the team took the guitar and drum back to the music room. They tied up the jobs from the show. Sara put the cups in the kitchen, and Joon folded the blanket. Mina put the paper plan on the wall.
Ms Park asked the class to talk about the power problem. Some children wanted music that did not depend on a computer. Mina wrote their ideas on the board. The class chose a new music club.
The children moved around the room and tested easy things. A bottle, a box, a spoon, and a bell made surprising music. The young boy taught a slow beat. Sara wrote a new plan.

A family at the library heard about the club and gave the school an old piano. Ms Park checked the piano and called in a piano man. The man fixed the keys. The class chose a place for it by the window.

At the new club, Mina looked at the dark computer and smiled. The power problem had changed their music, but it had not ended it. Guitar, cups, boxes, bells, hands, and children filled the room. The team began a new practice.
